aboutPage.title: About
aboutPage.intro: EverythingSkill.net is an open-source AI Skill discovery and sharing platform.
aboutPage.originBody1: In 2025, the .skill file format exploded across AI communities. It started with Colleague.skill, where someone distilled a real coworker into AI. Soon after, bosses, exes, celebrities, and even the self were being distilled into Skills.
aboutPage.originBody2: We believe everything can be distilled into a Skill. Every experience, personality, and knowledge system can become a reusable .skill file.
aboutPage.discoverBody: Browse the best open-source Skills by category.
aboutPage.shareBody: Submit your Skill and let more people benefit.
aboutPage.learnBody: Understand how .skill files work and how to create your own.
aboutPage.thanksBody: Thanks to every open-source Skill creator for making this community worth exploring. Special thanks to
aboutPage.thanksTail: for collecting and amplifying community Skills.

guidePage.metaTitle: What is an Agent Skill? Complete Guide to SKILL.md | EverythingSkill
guidePage.metaDesc: Learn what an Agent Skill is, how SKILL.md works, which platforms support it, and how to create your first skill. The complete open-format guide on EverythingSkill.net.
guidePage.heroSubtitle: A complete guide to SKILL.md — the open format for packaging AI knowledge, personas, and capabilities that works across 25+ platforms.
guidePage.s1Body1: An Agent Skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file — a Markdown document that teaches an AI agent how to perform a specific task, adopt a persona, or follow a repeatable workflow.
guidePage.s1Body2: Think of it as an AI 'personality plugin': you upload a skill, and the agent instantly knows how to think, respond, and act in that domain. A skill can distill any person's knowledge, any workflow, or any domain expertise into a reusable AI capability — and the same file works across every compatible platform.
guidePage.s1Rule: A skill is a file. No SDK, no API integration, no deployment pipeline.
guidePage.s2Body: Without skills, every conversation starts from zero. You re-explain team conventions, domain knowledge, and workflows every single time. Skills solve this permanently by packaging that context as reusable, version-controlled files.
guidePage.s2f1Desc: Package specialized knowledge into reusable instructions — legal review processes, data analysis pipelines, financial modeling workflows, or any persona.
guidePage.s2f2Desc: Give agents abilities they don't have out of the box — creating presentations, processing PDFs, building MCP servers, analyzing datasets with custom schemas.
guidePage.s2f3Desc: Turn multi-step tasks into consistent, auditable processes. A skill for database migrations always follows the same validation steps.
guidePage.s2f4Desc: Write a skill once and use it across Claude, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, and 25+ other compatible platforms without modification.
guidePage.s2f5Desc: Capture institutional knowledge in version-controlled packages. When someone leaves the team, their expertise stays in the skills they wrote.
guidePage.s3Intro: Skills use a 3-level progressive loading architecture to keep context efficient — loading only what's needed, when it's needed.
guidePage.s3L1Desc: At startup, the agent loads only the name and description from every available skill. These are injected into the system prompt so the agent always knows what skills exist and when they're relevant — with minimal context cost.
guidePage.s3L2Desc: When a user's request matches a skill's description, the agent reads the full SKILL.md body into context. This is where the real instructions, workflows, best practices, and examples live.
guidePage.s3L3Desc: Skills can bundle supporting files — scripts, reference docs, templates, schemas. These are loaded only when the SKILL.md instructions reference them, keeping context costs low.
guidePage.s4Intro: Every skill starts with a SKILL.md file containing YAML frontmatter followed by Markdown content. The frontmatter tells the agent what the skill is; the Markdown body tells it what to do.
guidePage.s4NameDesc: Max 64 characters. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only. Must match the parent directory name. No consecutive hyphens, cannot start or end with a hyphen.
guidePage.s4DescDesc: Max 1,024 characters. Describe what the skill does AND when to activate it. Both parts are essential for reliable skill discovery.
guidePage.s4LicenseDesc: License name (e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0) or path to a bundled license file.
guidePage.s4CompatDesc: Environment requirements — specific platform, required packages, network access, etc.
guidePage.s4MetaDesc: Arbitrary key-value map for additional properties such as author, version, or homepage.
guidePage.s4Tip: The description field is the most critical part of any skill. It's what the agent uses to decide whether to activate the skill. Always include both what the skill does AND when to use it.
guidePage.s5Intro: Agent Skills are an open standard originally developed by Anthropic. The same SKILL.md file works across 25+ AI development tools and agents without any modification.
guidePage.s6Intro: Creating a skill takes just a few minutes. You only need a text editor.
guidePage.s6Step1Desc: Create a folder named after your skill. Use only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens (e.g. my-skill, code-review, pdf-processing).
guidePage.s6Step2Desc: Add YAML frontmatter at the top with the required name and description fields. Write your instructions in Markdown below the frontmatter separator.
guidePage.s6Step3Desc: For complex skills, add scripts/ for executable code, references/ for documentation, and assets/ for templates and static resources.
guidePage.s6Step4Desc: Copy the skill folder into the appropriate directory for your platform. Project-level skills are shared with your team via git; user-level skills stay personal.
guidePage.s7Intro: Skills and MCP (Model Context Protocol) are complementary technologies that solve different problems. Many real workflows use both.
guidePage.s7Together: Together: A skill can reference MCP tools by fully-qualified name (e.g. BigQuery:query). Both can work within the same agent for the same task.
guidePage.faq1q: Do I need to code to create a skill?
guidePage.faq1a: No. A skill is just a Markdown file. If you can write a text document, you can create a skill. No SDK, no build step, no deployment.
guidePage.faq2q: Can I use the same skill across Claude, Cursor, and OpenAI Codex?
guidePage.faq2a: Yes. The SKILL.md format is an open standard supported by 25+ platforms. Write once, deploy anywhere — copy the same folder into each tool's skills directory.
guidePage.faq3q: What's the difference between a skill and a system prompt?
guidePage.faq3a: A system prompt is a static instruction block that's always loaded. A skill is a structured package that agents load on demand — only when relevant to the current task. Multiple skills can coexist without bloating context.
guidePage.faq4q: How many skills can I install?
guidePage.faq4a: As many as you like. Since only metadata (~100 tokens per skill) is loaded at startup, dozens of skills carry minimal context cost. Full instructions only load when the skill is actually triggered.
guidePage.faq5q: What kinds of skills can I create?
guidePage.faq5a: Any kind. Technical skills (code review, PDF processing, testing), workflow skills (database migrations, deployments), and persona skills (colleagues, celebrities, historical figures) — anything can be distilled into a skill.
guidePage.faq6q: Where can I find skills to install?
guidePage.faq6a: Browse the EverythingSkill library to discover 79+ open-source skills. You can also find skills on GitHub or create your own from scratch.
